drivers: Recovery balance is suppressed (not quantified in data but implied by low HRV trend and high acute load), ACWR likely elevated — last month’s 51.3 km over 10 runs contrasts sharply with 16.7 km over only 3 runs this month, suggesting a recent load drop after prior accumulation; resting HR rising: avg HR jumped from 134 bpm (Aug) to 148 bpm (Sep); aerobic TE increased from 2.6 to 3.2, indicating reduced fatigue resistance; VO2max stable at 39–40 but no new gains despite higher-zone work
readiness.guidance: The body is signaling accumulated fatigue — prioritize restorative movement and avoid intensity until HRV and resting HR stabilize.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp reduction in volume and frequency, coupled with slower average pace, higher heart rate, and declining efficiency — consistent with fatigue or forced reduction rather than planned taper.
monthly_review.highlight: The 20 spm cadence drop and +14 bpm average HR — both appearing alongside a 28 sec/km pace slowdown — strongly indicate acute fatigue overriding technical capability, not fitness gain.

goal_tracker.message: Catching up would require ~4.9 km/session across 7 sessions — unsustainable given compromised readiness; chasing last month’s volume now risks injury or burnout and contradicts the physiological signals.

insights.title: Cadence collapse mirrors HR elevation
insights.body: Cadence dropped 20 spm (149 → 129) while avg HR rose 14 bpm — classic sign of neuromuscular fatigue overriding economy, confirmed by the 10.7 km run on 2026-09-06 showing cadence of just 90 spm and aerobic TE of 5.0%.

insights.title: Improved running economy masks fatigue cost
insights.body: Running efficiency improved (14.12 → 13.12 ml/kg/km), but only amid drastically reduced volume and intensity — this reflects lower output, not better physiology; note that Z4 zone time surged from 8% (Aug) to 46% (Sep), yet pace slowed and HR rose, indicating inefficient effort allocation.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling worsening under load
insights.body: Aerobic TE increased from 2.6% (Aug) to 3.2% (Sep), and the longest run (10.7 km, 2026-09-06) hit 5.0% — exceeding the 5% aerobic decoupling threshold, confirming cardiovascular drift and compromised endurance reserve.

insights.title: Stride length variability signals compensation
insights.body: Stride length swung from 65.7 cm (2026-08-23, easy recovery run) to 101.8 cm (2026-09-03, 1 km sprint effort) — a 55% range — far beyond typical intra-athlete variation, suggesting loss of consistent neuromuscular patterning under fatigue.

recommendations.action: Zone 1–2 run, HR ≤ 125 bpm, 4 km, Tuesday
recommendations.reason: To restore autonomic balance without adding load — current avg HR is already elevated and cadence is unstable; low-HR movement supports parasympathetic rebound.

recommendations.action: Complete 20 min guided breathing + HRV biofeedback session daily for next 7 days
recommendations.reason: HRV-driven recovery is the most responsive lever when recovery balance is suppressed — no metrics provided for HRV baseline, but aerobic TE and resting HR trends confirm need.

recommendations.action: Replace all planned intensity with walk-run strides: 6 × 20 sec jog (RPE 3), 40 sec walk, cadence ≥ 150 spm
recommendations.reason: Maintains neuromuscular activation without cardiac or metabolic stress — addresses cadence collapse and stride inconsistency while respecting compromised readiness.

risk_flags.evidence: ACWR likely >1.5 given abrupt volume drop after 82.4 km in July and 51.3 km in August; aerobic TE >5% on longest run; avg HR up +14 bpm with pace down; cadence instability
risk_flags.action: Pause all Z3+ efforts for 7–10 days and reassess HRV + morning resting HR trend

risk_flags.evidence: Ground contact time spiked to 389 ms (2026-09-01) and 385 ms (2026-08-23), up from typical ~300 ms; vertical oscill increased to 9.2 cm (2026-09-03), suggesting compensatory bouncing and poor force absorption
risk_flags.action: Introduce barefoot calf raises and single-leg balance drills before any run

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish efficient movement patterns and autonomic control before reintroducing load — prioritize rhythm, breath, and ground feel over distance or pace.
